content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Spokane

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's specific requirements for your background—typically a secondary degree plus years of professional project hours, or a bachelor's degree plus fewer hours. Granite PM Academy's advisors can clarify your standing before enrollment.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Boot Camp. Our Spokane-based cohorts meet on a schedule that fits working professionals—attend real-time sessions with certified instructors who cover all five process groups and knowledge areas required by PMI.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the boot camp, complete your official PMI credential application and submit proof of your 35 contact hours from Granite PM Academy. Pay the exam fee directly to PMI at the time of application. Your application will be reviewed and either approved or audited by PMI.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Once approved by PMI, schedule your exam at a local Pearson VUE testing center in Spokane or take it remotely. Granite PM Academy provides exam-preparation materials, practice tests, and Q&A sessions to strengthen your readiness before test day.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, your PMP is valid for three years. During that cycle, earn professional development units (PDUs) by attending training, conferences, or publishing—Granite PM Academy's advanced courses and community events can help you accumulate the PDUs required for renewal.
